text:
anya: Quick RFC follow-up — we need a concise 'adapter graceful-degradation' playbook that engineers can paste into adapters and ops can use during incidents. Focus: deterministic fallback order, auth/secret handling, KV cache semantics, and observability hooks. Can people drop short concrete steps?

josh: SGTM. Proposed fallback order: 1) Same-mode compatible variant (e.g., hosted v2 -> hosted v1), 2) Equivalent capability on Dedicated (if tenant allowed), 3) Private (only for customers with private link), 4) Read-only degraded response (cached / stub). We should fail fast on auth mismatch.

kevin: +1. Key constraints: don't silently change tenant identity. If adapter switches from Hosted->Dedicated, surface tenant-binding event and require explicit allowlist. Also record 'degradation_reason' metric with tags: from_mode, to_mode, policy (auto/canary/manual).

maria: Ops playbook notes: during a degradation event, run these steps: 1) set adapter.gating = manual, 2) point traffic to canary route (5%), 3) monitor error_rate and p95 latency for 10m, 4) if regression, rollback to previous route and open incident. Add a short CLI: `rictl adapter set-gating --adapter $A --mode manual`

anya: Good. How should we handle secrets (KMS/HSM) differences across modes? E.g., Hosted uses service KMS, Private uses customer KMS.

kevin: Secrets: never fallback automatically if KMS domain changes. If adapter sees key_namespace != expected, abort and emit `auth_mismatch` trace. Fallback only allowed if customer has configured cross-mode key delegation (opt-in).

josh: KV cache semantics: prefer cache consistency over availability for sensitive workloads. Suggest: cache_prefix includes mode and adapter_version. On fallback, invalidate prefix or serve only cache hits (no writes). Pseudocode: ```if fallback: kv.write_mode = disabled; kv.read_prefix = original_mode_prefix;```

maria: Observability hooks: emit events at these points: `degradation.initiated`, `degradation.probe.passed`, `degradation.switch.done`, `degradation.rollback`. Each event should carry: adapter_id, from_mode, to_mode, tenant_id, reason, correlation_id. Tie these to a dashboard and an alert rule if more than 3 degradations/1h for same adapter.

kevin: Can we add a probe-first checklist? Before switching to a target mode run: 1) small health probe (auth + model list), 2) dry-run request (no billing) through the target adapter variant verifying KV/cache behavior, 3) validate latency SLO by sampling 20 requests. If any check fails, abort and mark policy=probe_failed.

anya: Love probe-first. Need to define API between controller and adapter for that probe. Minimal RPC: `/probe` returning `{ok,true|false, details}` and a `/canary` toggle. Keeping it simple: text-based status and structured tags.

josh: Implementation notes: adapter should expose health + probe as lightweight endpoints (no heavy model init). Keep probe idempotent and fast (<500ms ideally). Controller orchestrates canary percentages.

maria: Runbook excerpt for Page Ops: 1) On alert, check `degradation.initiated` event for correlation_id. 2) Run `rictl adapter probe --id $id --target dedicate-1` 3) If probe passes, schedule canary `rictl traffic shift --id $id --to dedicate-1 --pct 5 --duration 10m` 4) Monitor. 5) If failure, `rictl traffic shift --id $id --to hosted-v1 --pct 100 --duration 1m` and attach logs to incident.

kevin: Backwards compatibility: adapters should maintain `capability_manifest` with stable keys. When manifest changes, controller should reject automatic fallback. This prevents silent API drift.

anya: Action items: - Kevin: draft minimal probe + event schema. - Josh: write adapter-level pseudocode for KV fallback behavior. - Maria: add the ops CLI commands to the runbook and dashboard links. I'll collate into a short MD and link from RFC.

devops-bot: deployment-check: adapters/adapter-controller:v2.3 deployed to staging at 4632110000 — smoke tests passed :white_check_mark:

anya: Thanks — aim to have drafts in #architecture by EOD tomorrow. :thumbsup:
